items.title: Calculation of Relative Molecular Mass (Mᵣ) of a Gas

source_refs.note: Calculation of Relative Molecular Mass (Mᵣ) of a Gas: a main subheading of 5.2 Ideal gas equation, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 97-97.

blocks.text: Equation (4) can be employed to calculate the relative molecular mass of a gas whose P, T, V and mass in grams are known. This is achieved by rearranging equation (4)
Putting n = m/M in equation (4) Where m = mass in g and M = molar mass of the gas
At molecular level, the molar mass becomes relative molecular mass of a compound, therefore, we can write
The volume of 134 g of a gas at -73 ℃ under 10 atm pressure is 5 dm³. Determine the relative molecular mass of the gas.
Solution: The molecular mass of the gas can be calculated by using the formula:
M = (134 g)(0.0821 atm dm³ mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)(200 K) / (10 atm)(5 dm³)
Therefore, the relative molecular mass of the gas is 44 amu.

blocks.prompt: a) Explain why gases can be compressed easily?
blocks.explanation: Gas molecules are very far apart and about 99.9% of the volume of a gas is empty space. On compression the molecules simply come closer together into this empty space, so a gas is compressed easily.
When a compressed gas is allowed to expand suddenly, it cools. This cooling on sudden expansion is called the Joule-Thomson effect.

blocks.prompt: c) The volume of 21g a gas is 8 dm³ at -90 ºC under 7 atm pressure. Calculate the relative molecular mass of the gas.
blocks.explanation: T = −90 + 273 = 183 K. M = mRT/PV = (21 × 0.0821 × 183) / (7 × 8) = 315.5 / 56 = 5.6 g mol⁻¹. The relative molecular mass is about 5.6.
